subtype: Approach: finding a game they can play together [Thinking]
passage: It had been raining all day, and there was only one game console in the house. Salma and her brother Harsha both wanted the controller. "My turn!" "No, mine!" They were about to start again when Salma stopped and looked at the shelf. "We keep asking whose turn it is," she said. "That's the wrong question. What could the two of us play together?" Harsha blinked. "There's the racing game that has two controllers." They plugged in the second one, sat side by side, and spent the afternoon racing each other around the track, laughing about who crashed into the barrier the most.

qa.q: What kind of game did Harsha and Salma choose?
qa.a: They chose the racing game with two controllers.

qa.q: How did Salma feel about the fight over turns?
qa.a: Salma was frustrated that they kept asking whose turn it was and decided it was the wrong question; she wanted something the two of them could play together.

qa.q: What alternative approach could they use if the two-player game becomes boring, and why?
qa.a: They could use a timer to share turns or choose a board game. Either gives a fair option without a fight.

qa.q: How might Harsha see Salma's new question?
qa.a: Harsha blinked, then found the racing game right away, so Harsha probably felt surprised and happy to swap arguing for playing together.

grounding: Instead of fighting over the game, two siblings choose a two-player game, reframing the problem from whose turn to what they can do together.

subtype: Approach: finding a game they can play together [Thinking]
passage: Charu and Bhavna had fought over the single video game controller all Saturday morning in their flat in Andheri. "You've had three races!" "You had the last level!" Their mother had taken the batteries out. So the sisters sat on the floor, cross and bored. Charu picked up the game box and turned it over. "Hey. It says two players. We never tried that." "There's only one controller." "There's the old one in the drawer." Bhavna dug it out. Five minutes later they were side by side, racing and yelling at the same screen. When their mother walked past, she heard laughing instead of shouting and quietly put the batteries back on the table.

qa.q: Where did Bhavna find the second controller?
qa.a: She found the old one in the drawer.

qa.q: How did the sisters feel before Charu read the game box?
qa.a: They felt cross and bored after the fight and after their mother took the batteries out.

qa.q: What else could they try if a game has no two-player mode?
qa.a: They could pick an offline game both enjoy, like carrom, so they play together instead of waiting for turns.

qa.q: How does the change look to their mother?
qa.a: Their mother hears laughing instead of shouting, so she feels relieved and quietly gives the batteries back.

grounding: It shows two siblings switching from fighting over turns to choosing a two-player game they can play together.

passage:
"Give it! It's my turn!"
"You played for ages, Zeenat!"
"Mehak didi, you always say that."
"Because it's always true!"
They both fell back on the bed, glaring at the ceiling.
"This is so boring," Mehak said.
"Fighting is boring," Zeenat said. "Waiting is boring. Why are we even taking turns?"
"Because it's a one-person game."
"So pick a game where it's not."
"Like what?"
"That puzzle one. The one where you move the boxes and I jump."
"We need to talk to each other for that."
"So we talk."
Twenty minutes later: "Jump now! No, now!"

qa.a: She suggested the puzzle one where one moves the boxes and the other jumps.

qa.q: How did Zeenat feel just before she asked why they were taking turns?
qa.a: Zeenat felt bored and fed up with the fighting, which pushed her to think about the problem differently.

qa.q: What else could the sisters do if they still want to play the one-person game?
qa.a: They could use a timer for that game and save the two-player game for when both want to play at once.

qa.q: How does the new game look to Mehak?
qa.a: Mehak is unsure at first because they will need to talk, but soon she is shouting instructions and having fun.

grounding: It shows two siblings reframing a fight over turns into finding a game they can both play together.
